stories.headline: Amazon Agrees to Acquire Globalstar for $11.57B, Becomes Apple's Primary Satellite Provider

key_facts.fact: Amazon will pay $11.57 billion for Globalstar, or $90 per share in cash or Amazon stock, contingent on Globalstar meeting certain HIBLEO-4 replacement satellite milestones
As part of the deal, Amazon signed an agreement with Apple to become the primary satellite service provider for iPhone and Apple Watch, continuing existing out-of-cell-range connectivity
Amazon Leo (formerly Project Kuiper) aims to deploy over 7,700 LEO satellites but has only launched about 180 so far; Globalstar brings an existing operational satellite network and spectrum rights
Apple holds a 20% equity stake in Globalstar and has reserved 85% of its network capacity for iPhone emergency services after investing ~$1.5B in 2024
The acquisition intensifies competition with SpaceX's Starlink, which has over 10 million active users, ~10,000 satellites in orbit, and is adding ~52,000 new users per day
Amazon also unveiled the Leo Aviation Antenna, delivering up to 1 Gbps download and 400 Mbps upload for in-flight Wi-Fi, with Delta Air Lines among early adopters

stories.headline: Anthropic Largely Left European Regulators Out of Loop on Mythos Model Restrictions

key_facts.fact: Anthropic largely left European regulators out of the loop as it limited Mythos' release to select companies and organizations. The UK's AI Security Institute tested it, but EU regulatory bodies were not similarly engaged.
UK financial regulators (Bank of England, FCA, HM Treasury) are holding urgent talks with banks and the National Cyber Security Centre about risks from Mythos' vulnerability discovery capabilities.
Canada's AI Minister Evan Solomon announced a meeting with Anthropic senior leadership; the Bank of Canada and major lenders also met to discuss Mythos cybersecurity risks.
Previously, US Treasury Secretary Bessent and Fed Chair Powell summoned Wall Street bank CEOs for urgent discussions about Mythos and similar AI models' cybersecurity implications.
Anthropic said Mythos had identified 'thousands of high-severity vulnerabilities, including some in every major operating system and web browser,' some undetected for decades.

stories.headline: Cloudflare Launches Agent Cloud Platform With Sandboxes, New Runtime, and GPT-5.4 Access

key_facts.fact: Cloudflare expanded its Agent Cloud with Dynamic Workers (millisecond-start runtime for AI-generated code), general availability of Sandboxes (full Linux environments), and Artifacts (Git-compatible storage layer for agent-created code).

The platform introduced Think, a framework within its Agents SDK for longer-running, multi-step tasks that persist across sessions, targeting agents that continue work over time rather than respond to single prompts.

The expanded model catalogue includes OpenAI's GPT-5.4 and Codex following Cloudflare's acquisition of Replicate, enabling developers to choose between proprietary and open-source models on one platform.

CEO Matthew Prince: 'We are entering a world where agents are the ones writing and executing code. But agents need a home that is secure by default, scales to millions instantly, and persists across long-running tasks.'
OpenAI's Rohan Varma (Product, Codex) endorsed the partnership: 'Cloud agents are quickly becoming a foundational building block for how work gets done.'

stories.headline: EU's Iran War Energy Bill Hits €22B as Von der Leyen Calls Nuclear Phase-Out a 'Strategic Mistake'

key_facts.fact: The EU has spent an additional €22 billion on fossil fuels since the US-Israeli strikes on Iran began on February 28, amounting to roughly €500 million per day in extra costs
European Commission President von der Leyen said abandoning nuclear was a 'strategic mistake' and declared renewables and nuclear would be 'at the heart' of weaning Europe off oil and gas
The European Commission is expected to approve France's plan to build six new reactors at a cost of €70 billion; several other EU states are unpicking legal moratoriums on nuclear energy
Germany's coalition government agreed to give consumers and businesses about €1.6 billion in fuel price relief to respond to the oil price surge
ECB Vice President de Guindos said any ECB rate rise will depend on how war-driven surges in crude oil and chemical costs pass through to other prices
Several African countries including Tanzania and Kenya are bracing for 30% fuel price hikes at the pump due to the global energy disruption

stories.headline: FDA Approves First-Ever Drug for FSGS Kidney Disease, Travere's Filspari

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved Filspari (sparsentan) as the first and only medicine ever approved for focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), a rare kidney disease that scars filtering units
The approval is for adults and children aged 8+ with FSGS without nephrotic syndrome, expanding Filspari's total addressable population to more than 100,000 patients in the US
In the Phase 3 DUPLEX study (371 patients), Filspari showed a 48% reduction in proteinuria at Week 108 in non-nephrotic patients vs 27% for irbesartan (p=0.0075)
Travere prices Filspari at $9,900/month (~$170,000/year) for IgAN; Jefferies expects peak FSGS sales to reach $961 million by 2033
FSGS affects more than 40,000 patients in the US with a similar prevalence in Europe; the disease can lead to kidney failure if untreated

stories.headline: Missouri Voters Oust All 4 Council Incumbents After $6B Data Center Approval

key_facts.fact: All four incumbent Festus, Missouri city council members running for reelection were voted out one week after the council voted 6-2 to approve a $6 billion data center on 360 wooded acres.
Voter turnout was 129% higher than the April 2025 municipal election. First-time candidate Rick Belleville, 70, won by almost 45%.

The project, led by Clayco's development arm CRG, has an undisclosed Fortune 100 end user (codenamed 'Project Cumulus'). A lawsuit was filed alleging secret meetings, inadequate public notice, and Sunshine Law violations.
Records requests surfaced texts in which unnamed city figures referred to critics as 'uneducated people' and discussed a 'need to keep the flock herded.'

Activists with Wake Up JeffCo are gathering signatures to recall the mayor and remaining council members. The group Data Center Watch counts 188 organized opposition groups across 40 states, with $162 billion in halted or delayed projects.

stories.headline: Global Semiconductor Equipment Sales Hit Record $135.1B in 2025, Up 15%

key_facts.fact: Worldwide semiconductor manufacturing equipment sales rose 15% to a record $135.1 billion in 2025, up from $117.1 billion in 2024, driven by AI-related capacity investment.
The growth was driven by investment in advanced logic, memory, and AI-related capacity as chip companies accelerate fab buildouts to meet demand.
SEMI had previously reported 10% growth in global semiconductor equipment sales for 2024, reaching the prior record of $117.1 billion.
ASML, the sole manufacturer of EUV lithography tools, enters Q1 2026 earnings (April 15) with a $38.8 billion order backlog and expected revenue of $10.1-10.2 billion for the quarter.

stories.headline: Handshake's AI Data Labeling Revenue Hits ~$1B Run Rate, Up From $5M a Year Ago

key_facts.fact: Handshake's gross annualized revenue from AI data labeling hit approximately $1 billion, up from $550 million in January and just $5 million a year ago.
Mercor, another data labeling startup, also reached a $1B+ gross annualized revenue pace in 2026, reflecting surging demand for human contractors to train AI models.
Handshake was originally a successful career platform for early-career hiring, founded by Garrett Lord. Its pivot to AI data labeling has driven explosive revenue growth.

stories.headline: 100+ Robots at Hong Kong Exhibition as China Scales Humanoid Mass Production

key_facts.fact: More than 100 robots were showcased at two exhibitions starting Monday at the Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Center, demonstrating capabilities from conversation and boxing to backflips and security patrol.

China had more than 140 humanoid-robot manufacturers and 330+ models in 2025. Omdia ranked AGIBOT, Unitree Robotics, and UBTech as the only first-tier vendors globally, each shipping over 1,000 units in 2025, with AGIBOT and Unitree exceeding 5,000 units each.
EngineAI's Robert Chan said the company plans to launch two factories in China for mass production this year, noting China's advantages in low-cost engineering and industry know-how sharing.

Shenzhen launched its first pilot production line specifically for humanoid robots on April 12, assembling Leju Robotics' Roban 2 in about two hours per unit. A mass production facility in Foshan targets 10,000+ units per year.
Unitree Robotics listed its R1 humanoid on AliExpress for $6,800-$8,100, targeting global consumers. The company shipped 5,500 humanoid units in 2025 and targets 20,000 in 2026.
Shenzhen DX Intech sold more than 400 hyper-realistic female humanoid robots with soft synthetic faces, signaling a move toward emotional and lifelike interaction.

stories.headline: IEA: Iran War Will Cause First Annual Oil Demand Decline Since COVID-19 Pandemic

key_facts.fact: IEA now projects global oil demand will contract by 80,000 bpd in 2026, a 730,000 bpd swing from its March forecast of 640,000 bpd growth
A projected 1.5 million bpd drop in demand in Q2 2026 would mark the deepest quarterly contraction since the COVID-19 pandemic
Global oil supply plummeted by 10.1 million bpd in March to 97 million bpd — the largest supply disruption in history, according to the IEA
OPEC+ production fell 9.4 million bpd month-on-month to 42.4 million bpd; Middle East and Asia refineries cut crude runs by 6 million bpd in April
In a worst-case scenario with prolonged disruptions, the IEA projects demand could fall 5 million bpd year-on-year and nearly 2 billion barrels would be drawn from stocks
Deepest demand cuts so far have hit Middle East and Asia-Pacific, mainly naphtha, LPG, and jet fuel; demand destruction expected to spread as scarcity persists

stories.headline: Intel Adds $100B+ in Market Value in Record 53% Nine-Day Rally on Terafab, Google Deals

key_facts.fact: Intel shares soared 53% in nine sessions including Monday, the largest such rally on record for the company, adding more than $100 billion in market value and pushing its market cap above $325 billion.
Intel joined Elon Musk's Terafab project to develop semiconductors for Tesla, SpaceX and xAI, followed by Google committing to use future Intel Xeon processors in data centers.
Intel agreed to buy back a 49% stake in its Ireland Fab 34 from Apollo Global Management for $14.2 billion, signaling a shift from survival mode to expansion mode.
The US government's stake in Intel is now worth roughly $27 billion, more than three times its original investment.
Intel's stock is up 72% year-to-date after an 84% jump in 2025 but trades at over 90x estimated forward earnings, its highest on record. Only 10 of 52 analysts have buy ratings.
Benchmark raised its price target to $76 and Cantor Fitzgerald to $60. Intel reports Q1 earnings on April 23.

stories.headline: Lucid Secures $750M Funding; Uber to Buy 35K+ Additional Vehicles, Expands Investment to $500M

key_facts.fact: Uber agreed to purchase at least 35,000 additional Lucid vehicles for its robotaxi fleet and invest $200 million more, taking its total Lucid investment to $500 million
Lucid secured $750 million in total new funding and named a new CEO as part of the announcement
Uber has begun early employee test rides of Lucid Gravity robotaxis equipped with Nuro's Level 4 autonomous driving technology in the San Francisco Bay Area
Uber has committed to deploying up to 20,000 Lucid Gravity SUVs converted to robotaxis using Nuro's autonomous platform, with manufacturing expected to start at Lucid's Arizona factory late 2026
The Lucid Gravity robotaxis are equipped with Nvidia Drive AGX Thor computers, high-resolution cameras, solid-state lidar, and radar for Nuro's autonomous driving system

stories.headline: Markets Rally and Oil Falls Below $100 as Blockade Begins but US-Iran Dialogue Stays Alive

key_facts.fact: Brent crude fell nearly 2% to $97.50/barrel and WTI dropped 2.27% to $96.83 on Tuesday, reversing Monday's 4%+ spike, after both sides signaled openness to renewed talks
The S&P 500 rose 1% to close at 6,886 on Monday; Japan's Nikkei 225 surged 2.5% and South Korea's KOSPI jumped 3.7% on Tuesday
The US blockade went into effect Monday at 5:30pm Iranian time; at least two tankers turned around, but a Chinese-owned tanker Rich Starry was the first to transit the strait after the blockade began
Pakistan's PM Sharif said efforts were still underway to resolve the conflict; Trump said Iran had called and 'would like to make a deal very badly'
ANZ analysts estimate ~10 million bpd of crude supply has been removed from the market, with a prolonged blockade potentially curbing an additional 3-4 million bpd
No NATO ally has joined the US blockade; the UK and France are co-hosting a 40+ nation summit this week to discuss restoring free transit through Hormuz independently

stories.headline: OpenAI Acquires AI Personal Finance Startup Hiro Finance in Acquihire Deal

key_facts.fact: OpenAI acquired Hiro Finance, an AI personal finance startup founded in 2023. Terms were not disclosed. Hiro will stop accepting new signups, shut down operations April 20, and delete all user data by May 13.
Hiro's ~10 employees will join OpenAI. The startup built an AI-powered financial planning tool that modeled 'what-if' scenarios for consumers using salary, debts, and expense data.
Founder Ethan Bloch previously founded Digit, a savings-focused fintech sold to Oportun for more than $200 million. Hiro was backed by Ribbit Capital, General Catalyst, and Restive.
This is not OpenAI's first financial app acquisition. The deal may be part of an effort to expand ChatGPT's financial capabilities and compete for agent-based finance use cases.

stories.headline: OpenAI Internal Memo Claims Anthropic Overstates Revenue by ~$8B via Cloud Partner Rev Share

key_facts.fact: OpenAI CRO Denise Dresser sent a four-page memo to employees saying Anthropic is 'grossing up rev share with Amazon and Google,' which overstates its run rate by roughly $8B against the stated $30B ARR figure.

Dresser wrote 'the market is as competitive as I have ever seen it' and that though Anthropic's 'coding focus gave them an early wedge,' 'you do not want to be a single-product company in a platform war.'
Dresser characterized Anthropic's positioning: 'Their story is built on fear, restriction, and the idea that a small group of elites should control AI.'

The memo pushes a platform strategy: 'Multi-product adoption makes us harder to replace... We should stop thinking like a company with separate product lines. We should think like a platform company.'
Dresser recently took over much of former COO Brad Lightcap's duties as he transitions to a new role focused on special projects. Both OpenAI and Anthropic reportedly plan to go public this year.

stories.headline: Oracle Expands Bloom Energy Partnership to 2.8 GW of Fuel Cells for AI Data Centers

key_facts.fact: Oracle and Bloom Energy expanded their partnership under a master services agreement for up to 2.8 GW of Bloom's solid oxide fuel cell systems to power AI and cloud infrastructure.
An initial 1.2 GW of capacity has been contracted, with deployment underway across Oracle projects in the US and continuing into next year.
Last year Bloom Energy delivered a fully operational fuel cell system to Oracle in just 55 days, over a month ahead of the expected 90-day deployment schedule.
Oracle received a warrant to purchase $400 million of Bloom Energy stock on April 9, on terms previously announced in October 2025.
Bloom Energy shares rose 6% to $176.67 in regular trading and surged to $198.65 in extended trading, up 12.6%. The stock has more than doubled in value this year.
Oracle stock surged 12.69% to $155.62 on Monday following the announcement, significantly outpacing the broader market.

stories.headline: Stanford AI Index 2026: US-China Model Gap Narrows to 2.7%, GenAI Adoption Outpaces PC and Internet

key_facts.fact: US and China are effectively tied on frontier model performance, with Anthropic leading by just 2.7% on Chatbot Arena as of March 2026; both countries have traded the top slot repeatedly since early 2025.
53% of the global population now uses generative AI regularly, reaching that penetration in three years — faster than the PC (~16 years) or the internet (~7 years).

Only 10% of Americans say they are more excited than concerned about AI in daily life, compared to 56% of AI experts who expect a positive impact. On jobs, the split is 73% expert optimism vs. 23% public.
Employment for software developers aged 22-25 has fallen nearly 20% since 2022, while the 35-to-49 cohort in the same field grew. The same divergence appears in customer service and paralegal work.

xAI's Grok 4 training emitted over 72,000 tons of CO2 (equivalent of 17,000 cars driving for a year); AI data center power capacity hit 29.6 GW; GPT-4o annual inference water use may exceed drinking water needs of 12 million people.
US private AI investment reached $109B in 2025. Over 90% of notable AI models now come from private companies. The US hosts 5,427 data centers — more than 10x any other country.
The US ranks just 24th globally in AI adoption at 28.3%. Southeast Asian nations — China, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore — report over 80% regular GenAI usage.
US public trust in government to regulate AI is the lowest among surveyed countries at 31%, compared to 81% in Singapore.

stories.headline: Uber and Lucid Expand Robotaxi Partnership to 35,000 Vehicles With $750M in New Investment

key_facts.fact: Uber and Lucid expanded their robotaxi partnership from 20,000 to at least 35,000 vehicles, including Lucid Gravity and upcoming Midsize models, for Uber's future global robotaxi service.

Uber committed an additional $200 million investment in Lucid, bringing its total investment to $500 million. Saudi Arabia's PIF (via Ayar Third Investment) committed a separate $550 million investment.
The companies plan commercial launch of their robotaxi service later this year in the San Francisco Bay Area using Lucid Gravity SUVs with Nuro's Level 4 autonomous driving technology.
Lucid also named Silvio Napoli (former CEO of Schindler Group) as permanent CEO, replacing interim CEO Marc Winterhoff who moves to COO.

Lucid's preliminary Q1 2026 results show revenue of $280-284 million, an operating loss of ~$1 billion, production of 5,500 vehicles, and deliveries of 3,093 units. Full-year production guidance of 25,000-27,000 vehicles was reaffirmed.

stories.headline: UK AI Security Institute: Claude Mythos Is First AI to Complete 32-Step Enterprise Attack Simulation

key_facts.fact: On expert-level CTF challenges — which no model could complete before April 2025 — Mythos Preview succeeded 73% of the time.

Claude Mythos Preview is the first AI model to solve 'The Last Ones' (TLO), a 32-step corporate network attack simulation, completing the full chain in 3 out of 10 attempts with an average of 22 out of 32 steps.
Claude Opus 4.6, the next best performing model, completed an average of only 16 steps on the same simulation. AISI estimates the exercise requires ~20 hours for human experts.
AISI emphasized the test environments lacked real-world defenses: no active monitoring, no intrusion detection, no incident response, and no human defenders.
Performance continued to scale with additional compute up to the 100M token budget tested, and AISI expects improvements to continue beyond that limit.
AISI noted the model failed to complete its operational technology focused range 'Cooling Tower', though it got stuck on IT sections rather than OT-specific tasks.

organizations: UK Department for Science, Innovation and Technology

stories.headline: China's YMTC Plans Two New Fabs to More Than Double Flash Memory Production

key_facts.fact: YMTC plans to build two additional factories on top of a third fab completing this year, which would more than double its production capacity once all three are operational.
Each of the three new fabs will have a capacity of 100,000 wafers per month at full utilization. YMTC's current two fabs produce 200,000 wafers per month combined.

YMTC's third fab in Wuhan should start production by end of 2026 and reach 50,000 wafers/month by 2027. The building is complete and equipment installation is underway, with over 50% of equipment sourced domestically.
YMTC held 11.8% of the global NAND flash market in 2025 according to UBS, with the firm projecting its share will exceed 14% by early 2027. Samsung leads at 30.4%.

All three new fabs will allocate part of their capacity to DRAM production, marking YMTC's expansion beyond NAND flash. The company has sent LPDDR samples to customers and expects mass production by year-end.

A bipartisan group of US lawmakers this month proposed the MATCH Act, which would ban the sale of older DUV lithography machines to Chinese chipmakers like YMTC, expanding existing export controls beyond EUV systems.
